## Natural history notes

A small aquatic leaf beetle characterized by its elongated body, long antennae, and metallic bronze, greenish, or dark coloration typical of many reed beetles. In Florida, it would be expected around ponds, marshes, wet prairies, canals, and other freshwater wetlands with emergent or floating aquatic plants. Adults feed on the exposed portions of aquatic plants, while the larvae develop on submerged plant tissues and are adapted to life in wetland vegetation, helping link aquatic plant growth with the broader insect food web.
